𝐌𝐚𝐤𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐌𝐨𝐬𝐭 𝐨𝐟 𝐋𝐚𝐰 𝐒𝐜𝐡𝐨𝐨𝐥: 𝐀 𝐒𝐞𝐬𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐑𝐞𝐜𝐚𝐩

The Internship and Placement Committee, SCLML Rashtriya Raksha University (INI), hosted an insightful session titled "Making the Most of Law School," delivered by Mr. Manuj Gupta , a fifth-year B.A. LL.B. (Hons.) student at National University of Juridical Sciences, Kolkata and an incoming Trainee Associate at A&O Shearman, London.

The conversation began with a reflection on how genuine interest is built not through effort alone, but through curiosity: asking questions, engaging with seniors and faculty, and surrounding oneself with people who are equally driven to learn and grow. This naturally led to a discussion on staying motivated in non-competitive spaces, where he spoke about the importance of taking the first step and creating your own space, even if that means actively seeking guidance from mentors, seniors, or professionals you admire, wherever you can find them.

On academic writing, he emphasised that true value lies in originality a paper should offer something genuinely novel to the field, rather than simply fulfilling a requirement. The discussion then moved to mooting, where his advice for first-timers was refreshingly simple: dive in headfirst. When it came to handling the pressure of oral rounds, he spoke about drawing confidence from the preparation already put in, and owning that space with clarity and self-assurance.

He closed with a strong endorsement of pursuing fellowships something he noted he missed out on during his own law school journey highlighting the real-world exposure, meaningful networks, and research grounding they offer.

Overall, it was a session less about building a resume and more about building the mindset behind one. Grateful to have been part of this conversation.
